lines.text: St. Matthew I1: 2-6
December II, 1938
Now when John heard in prison about the deeds of the Christ,
he sent word by his disciples and said to him, "Are you he who is
to come, or shall we look for another?" And Jesus answered them,
"Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind receive their
sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear,
and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news
preached to them. And blessed is he who takes no offence at me."
ADVENT, the time of preparation for the Feast of the Nativity,
the incarnation of the Word, confronts us with the question:
How shall I receive the Lord?
For the Third Sunday in Advent the Church chooses the
gospel concerning the question of John the Baptist, so that
from it we may learn the right way to prepare ourselves.
This gospel tells us how the Baptist, cast into prison by
Herod Antipas, sent two of his disciples to Jesus with the
question: "Are you he who is to come?" Many readers are
puzzled to know how the Baptist came to ask Jesus such a
question. Did he not already know Jesus? Must it be that
doubts arose in his mind with regard to Jesus? Or was it that
the disciples were to ask Jesus this question not to satisfy
any curiosity on the part of the Baptist, but for their own
good, that they might hear from the lips of Jesus Himself
that He was the One who should come? We do not
know and ought not to seek to know. The story is told
us only in order that we might hear this decisive question
and might make it our own: "Are you he who is to come?"
